s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of unilateral weakness, speech disturbance, and visual disturbance with a history of cardiac arrhythmia and pacemaker implantation
salient_findings: Gaze deviation in the right eye
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 70s
Presented to the emergency department
Has a history of permanent atrial fibrillation
Has a history of complete heart block
Has a pacemaker implanted in the late 1990s
Pacemaker was upgraded to a biventricular system
Blood pressure was 147/75 mm Hg
Heart rate was 84 beats per minute
Respiratory rate was 16 breaths per minute
Oxygen saturation was 99% on room air
Computed tomography angiography showed a large middle cerebral artery territory
Electrocardiogram showed a ventricular-paced rhythm with ventricular bigeminy

salient_findings: Gaze deviation in the right eye

differentials: Vasculitis of the central nervous system due to giant cell arteritis
Primary angiitis of the central nervous system
per_call: Vasculitis of the central nervous system due to giant cell arteritis
Primary angiitis of the central nervous system

shortlist.label: Ischemic stroke
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with unilateral weakness, speech disturbance, and visual disturbance, and computed tomography angiography showed a large middle cerebral artery territory

shortlist.label: Cardioembolic stroke
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of permanent atrial fibrillation and complete heart block, which increases the risk of cardioembolic stroke

shortlist.label: Middle cerebral artery occlusion
shortlist.why_kept: Computed tomography angiography showed a large middle cerebral artery territory, suggesting occlusion of the middle cerebral artery

shortlist.label: Lacunar stroke
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with unilateral weakness and speech disturbance, which are common symptoms of lacunar stroke

shortlist.label: Atrial fibrillation-related stroke
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of permanent atrial fibrillation, which increases the risk of atrial fibrillation-related stroke

raw.rationale: The patient's history of permanent atrial fibrillation and the presence of a large middle cerebral artery territory on computed tomography angiography support this diagnosis, as atrial fibrillation is a known risk factor for cardioembolic stroke.

rejected.label: Ischemic stroke
rejected.why: Too broad, as cardioembolic stroke is a subtype of ischemic stroke

rejected.label: Middle cerebral artery occlusion
rejected.why: More of a specific finding than a diagnosis

rejected.label: Lacunar stroke
rejected.why: Typically presents with smaller, deeper infarcts, not a large middle cerebral artery territory

rejected.label: Atrial fibrillation-related stroke
rejected.why: Essentially synonymous with cardioembolic stroke in this context, but cardioembolic stroke is more specific
